text:
mira: Heads-up — onboarding a new HF model (hf-org/sparse-embed-3b) and seeing weird reranker regressions after conversion. Embeddings look shifted vs HF tokenizer pooling. anyone seen CLS/mean/truncation mismatches cause MRR drops?

junaid: ugh. did you use the HF `config.json` -> `tokenizer_class` conversion tool or the fast path?

mira: converted with the usual script but noticed in the Redwood converted tokenizer `cls_token` is missing and we default to `\u0120` as pad in some cases. quick repro: embed pool mean vs cls gives ~8% MRR delta on our dev set.

sam: can you paste the config snippet? also, which truncation strategy did you pick — `longest_first` vs `only_first`? chat templates can change order.

mira: here's the relevant bits we ended up with (redacted):
```json
{
  "tokenizer_class": "BPETokenizer",
  "add_prefix_space": false,
  "cls_token": null,
  "pad_token": "\\u0120",
  "truncation_strategy": "longest_first",
  "model_max_length": 2048
}
```
I think HF had `cls_token` = "<CLS>" in the `special_tokens_map`, but the conversion didn't wire it. Also chat template uses `{{query}}\n--\n{{context}}` so the truncation side matters for reranking.

eval-bot: automated eval run ml-eval/2026-03-rerank-v2 finished. Baseline (hf-tokenizer+cls) MRR=0.412. Converted (rw-tokenizer, mean pool) MRR=0.379. Difference = -8.0%. Full log: https://ci.redwood/eng/ml/evals/2026-03-rerank-v2

junaid: that gap screams token alignment/prefix handling. If `cls_token` is null downstream pooling that expects an explicit CLS index will pick token 0 or last token. mean pool won't be comparable. Can you run a tiny repro that prints token ids and offsets for a couple queries?

mira: done. sample: 
```
query: "What is Redwood Optimize?"
hf tokens: [101, 759, 102, ...]
hf offsets: [(0,4),(5,9),(9,10),...]
rw tokens: [759, 102, ...]
rw offsets: [(0,4),(5,9),(9,10),...]
```
note HF preserved a leading CLS (101) while rw dropped it. So embedding index mapping shifts.

sam: that explains embedding mismatch. two immediate fixes: 1) ensure conversion injects `cls_token` into `special_tokens_map` and updates tokenizer.vocab/merges, or 2) change pooling config to use `mean_excluding_pad` and canonicalize inputs (i.e., add CLS token on encode). Also check `add_prefix_space` differences for BPE vs byte-level — it affects offsets.

kai: small note on truncation: if chat template concatenates query+context and we use `truncation_strategy: "longest_first"`, HF will trim from both sides which changes whether the CLS token gets pushed out. For rerank you want `only_second` (truncate context) or do truncation before adding CLS.

mira: great, I'll try two variants: re-run conversion with manual `special_tokens_map` injection, and change truncation to `only_second` + explicit `cls_token` insertion. I'll post the quick script I used.

mira: (later) quick script we used to reproduce:
```bash
python - <<'PY'
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('hf-org/sparse-embed-3b')
print('cls:', t.cls_token, 'pad:', t.pad_token, 'add_prefix_space', getattr(t, 'add_prefix_space', None))
print(t.encode('What is Redwood Optimize?'))
PY
```
this shows HF has `cls_token` but the rw-converter didn't.

junaid: can you file a small ticket on the conversion repo with the HF model link + your output? include the eval links. i'll triage and add a regression test for `cls_token` preservation + a tiny rerank smoke eval. cc @kai

mira: done — https://git.redwood/repo/conv/issues/412. added repro and eval link. thanks all :thumbsup:

sam: one more: when you run quantization experiments later, preserve the exact tokenization pipeline. int8 kernel changes are fine but token id order must be identical or bench comparisons are meaningless. learned that the hard way with a GPT-style embedder earlier.

kai: agreed. also add a short unit test that encodes a canonical test string and asserts first token == CLS when model expects it. saves us from future silent drift.

mira: will add tests + re-run ml-eval after conversion patch. closing loop when results are in.

eval-bot: queued eval ml-eval/2026-03-rerank-v2-repro for Mira's branch.
